title: The Basket of Apples (La Corbeille de pommes)

image.credit: Photograph via Wikimedia Commons (Paul Cézanne - The Basket of Apples - 1926.252 - Art Institute of Chicago.jpg)

source.label: The Basket of Apples (La Corbeille de pommes)

highlight.text: Closer looking reveals shifts in reality conveyed by the misaligned tabletop, tilted bottle, cascading apples, and the precarious tower of cookies known as langues de chat (cat tongues), which magically stop just short of falling out of the picture.

source.author: Art Institute of Chicago

work.text: Early on, he painted landscapes, the typical Impressionist subject, but his arresting and complex still lifes changed the traditional nature morte (dead nature) genre and continue to puzzle and tantalize today.

source.author: Art Institute of Chicago
source.title: The Basket of Apples (La Corbeille de pommes)

moment.text: In many ways Paul Cezanne was the odd man out among the artists branded as “Impressionists”—those who showed their works outside of France’s state-sponsored Salon exhibitions.

source.author: Art Institute of Chicago
source.title: The Basket of Apples (La Corbeille de pommes)

matters.text: Cezanne rarely signed his paintings, so his signature at the bottom left suggests the importance he ascribed to this painting or to its original owner.
